comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C30-C33 regarding native holdup benchmarking with DNM2. Both evaluations find the technique well-validated and supported by experimental data, though peer reviewer notes it is 'relatively unproven' while still acknowledging its capacity to measure relative affinity.

Strong agreement on claims C34-C36 regarding proteome-wide BIN1 SH3 interactome discovery. Both evaluations accept the nHU-MS data as solid evidence for an unexpectedly high number of cellular protein interactions. Peer review also includes C91 (summary claim) in their acceptance.

Agreement on claims C37-C38 regarding comparative SH3 domain analysis showing specificity differences. Peer review extends acceptance to include claims C50-C53 on motif preferences and specificity logos, praising the 'outstanding data' on binding properties of seven distinct SH3 domains.

Agreement on claims C40-C42 regarding identification of neuromuscular disorder-associated proteins as BIN1 partners. Peer review extends to include claims C80-C84 about SMCHD1 and other disease-linked proteins, finding this 'unexpected and interesting' for understanding muscle disease networks.

Agreement on claims C43-C46 regarding PRM identification and fragmentomic approach. Both evaluations support the systematic mapping of direct interactions through predicted PRMs. Peer review also includes claims C47-C49 on the finding that many partners lack detectable PRMs, noting the value of using both cell-derived proteins and peptides.

Divergence on claims C54-C57 regarding BIN1's role in mitosis and PRC1 interaction. OpenEval finds claims supported by functional enrichment and experimental data. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting findings are 'rather preliminary' and 'may necessitate additional experimental work to be more convincing,' particularly questioning PRC1's lower affinity compared to DNM2.

Divergence on claims C58-C63 regarding BIN1-PRC1 co-localization and mitotic observations. OpenEval finds claims supported by membrane tubulation, titration, and immunofluorescence data. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, stating the data is 'less convincing' or 'too preliminary,' noting PRC1's lower affinity and that localization data is insufficient to substantiate a mitotic role.

Agreement on claims C22, C25-C29 regarding cellular validation of BIN1 variants through membrane tubulation and holdup assays. Both evaluations accept the experimental evidence, including the acknowledged discrepancy between in vitro and cellular results for F584S. Peer review notes 'Generally, the data supports the conclusions.'

Agreement on claims C64-C67 regarding systematic variant effect measurement across 448 PRMs and interactome perturbations. Both evaluations accept the comprehensive characterization of variant effects. Peer review extends to include claims C87-C88, C93 on variant analysis contributions and novel insights into BIN1 cellular function.

Agreement on claims C68-C72 regarding structural analysis of variant effects using AlphaFold2, and claims C73-C75 on AlphaFold2 limitations. Both evaluations accept the structural rationalization and the conclusion that computational methods have limitations requiring experimental validation.

Agreement on claims C86, C89-C90 regarding the utility of affinity interactomics for variant characterization and potential for drug development. Both evaluations support the methodological contribution for detecting molecular phenotypes of rare variants, with peer review noting potential for 'new avenues in drug development efforts.'

Agreement on claims C1-C13 (background on BIN1 structure, function, disease associations) and partial overlap with claims C14-C24 (gaps in knowledge, study rationale). Both evaluations accept this established background literature as foundational context without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claim C85 regarding collective perturbation of multiple interactions contributing to CNM pathology. Both evaluations accept this inference as a reasonable conclusion from the demonstrated proteome-wide affinity perturbations caused by pathological variants.

Agreement on claims C76-C78 regarding established background on DNM2, PRC1, and cytokinesis. Both evaluations accept this cited literature. OpenEval also includes C79 on BIN1's involvement in cytokinesis, which peer review implicitly questions through their uncertainty about the mitotic role findings.

Strong agreement on claims C50-C53 regarding affinity-weighted specificity logos and motif preferences across multiple SH3 domains. Peer review praises the 'outstanding data' on binding properties showing 'surprising differences in the promiscuity' of these proteins.

Agreement on claims C47-C49 regarding the finding that many high-affinity partners lack detectable PRMs, revealing that SH3 interactions involve contributions beyond individual PxxP motifs. Peer review accepts this as part of the comprehensive fragmentomic approach.

Partial agreement on claims C80-C84 regarding SMCHD1 as a high-affinity partner linked to muscle disease. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to explicit speculation about disease role (C84). Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, finding the identification of disease-linked proteins 'unexpected and interesting,' though they don't specifically address the speculative disease mechanism.

Agreement on claims C14-C21 regarding gaps in knowledge about BIN1's interaction network and study rationale. Both evaluations accept this background context establishing the need for the current study, with peer review accepting the foundational literature without challenge.

Agreement on claim C91 (summary of proteome-wide interaction discovery). Both evaluations accept this as a major finding supported by nHU-MS data. OpenEval also includes C92-C93 on mitotic enrichment and variant effects, which peer review addresses separately with varying levels of acceptance.

Divergence on claim C92 regarding mitotic enrichment as a major finding. OpenEval finds this supported by functional enrichment analysis. Peer review rates the mitotic findings as UNCERTAIN and preliminary, requiring additional experimental work.

Agreement on claim C93 regarding variant interactome characterization as a major contribution. Both evaluations accept the fragmentomic holdup data for variants as providing novel insights into BIN1 cellular function.

Agreement on claim C39 regarding identification of numerous previously unknown BIN1 partners. Peer review implicitly accepts this through their acknowledgment of 'an unexpectedly high number' of new interactions representing 'an unexpected and interesting finding.'

Agreement on claims C73-C75 regarding AlphaFold2's failure to predict observed affinity perturbations and the conclusion that experimental approaches remain essential. Both evaluations accept this as an important negative result highlighting computational limitations.
